criteria.text: Starlette, Router, Mount and Route accept max_body_size; default None leaves arbitrarily large bodies accepted.

App-level limit applies before routing; a Route/Mount/Router limit higher than the outer one lets a body through that the outer limit would reject, a lower one rejects a body the outer limit would allow; routes without their own limit use the outer one.
RequestBodyLimitMiddleware wraps a plain (non-Starlette) ASGI app and returns 413 'Content Too Large' text/plain when the received body exceeds max_body_size, and passes bodies at or under the limit.
A body with absent or understated Content-Length that exceeds the limit is rejected; multipart bodies are counted in full including boundaries.

A declared Content-Length over the limit gets 413 without endpoint code running: the middleware rejects on entry; in Starlette the matched route's own limit (or outer, or app's for no-route/405) decides, so an inner route raising the limit allows the request.
If the app already started its response when the limit is crossed, no second response start is sent and the receive stream ends/disconnects.
When a multipart parse is interrupted by any exception (including body limit exceeded), all temporary files created are closed.
GET requests without a body, websocket connections and lifespan work unchanged when a limit is set.
Docs describe max_body_size on Starlette/Router/Mount/Route and RequestBodyLimitMiddleware.
Tests exist for app, router, mount, route (inner raise and lower), standalone middleware, Content-Length fail-fast, multipart, and temp-file cleanup.

intents.rationale: No max_body_size option exists on Starlette, Router, Mount or Route.
Needs a shared per-request limit state in scope: the app limit is installed before routing; Route/Mount/inner Router replace the limit when they handle a request.
Wrap receive to count http.request body bytes regardless of Content-Length.
Content-Length is checked on entry in the middleware, and in Starlette after routing settles (matched Route/Mount/Router handle, partial/405 match, or app limit before redirect/default/404).
Send 413 PlainTextResponse 'Content Too Large' if response not started; otherwise send nothing further and end the body stream (http.disconnect).
MultiPartParser.parse only closes files on MultiPartException/OSError; must close on any interruption, including body-limit exceptions and cancellation.
Limit logic applies only to scope type http; websocket and lifespan pass through untouched; requests with no body are never over a limit.
Document in docs/middleware.md, docs/applications.md and docs/routing.md.

summary: Single PR: a shared per-request body-limit state and middleware in starlette/middleware/body_limit.py, wired through Starlette/Router/Mount/Route with Content-Length checks deferred until routing settles, multipart temp-file cleanup hardened, plus docs and tests.

tasks.summary: Add starlette/middleware/body_limit.py with a per-request limit state (counts received http.request bytes, mutable limit, tracks response started, sends 413 'Content Too Large' once or ends the stream with http.disconnect if the response started) plus RequestBodyLimitMiddleware (http only, Content-Length checked on entry). Then thread max_body_size through Router.app, Route.handle, Mount.handle and Starlette; Content-Length is checked only after the applicable limit settles (matched route/mount/router, partial 405 match, or app limit before redirect/default/404). Harden MultiPartParser.parse to close files on any exception. Then add tests and docs.
